STOCKASTIC V2 Designs a film stock for one specific camera, and exports it as an OCIO configuration. This is not a grading tool and not a raw processor — the picture on screen is a preview of the configuration, and the configuration is the deliverable. Open a RAW from the camera you are designing for.

CREDITS

Generally inspired by the elegant work by Petrikas, Saulala — particularly the vibrancy slider, whose behaviour the vibrancy stage here was reverse-engineered from.

Big thanks to Troy Sobotka for creating AgX, which most of the function of this app and of Saulala is based on, and which is the entire reason I went down the rabbit hole of picture formation to begin with — as well as for patiently answering my questions about AgX and colour.

RAW decoding by LibRaw-Wasm (LibRaw, LGPL-2.1). Colour-management naming and aliases follow Blender’s OCIO config.

Building colour engine…
Opens camera raw directly — embedded LibRaw (LGPL-2.1, via libraw-wasm): CR2/CR3, NEF, ARW, RAF, ORF, RW2, PEF, DNG and more. Also linear EXR. Runs entirely in the browser; nothing is uploaded.

The picture-formation approach follows Troy Sobotka’s AgX and SB2383 work, with the per-channel hue handling after Eary Chow’s AgX. Gamut compression is Jed Smith’s algorithm (the ACES reference), implemented from Juan Pablo Zambrano’s DCTL port. Film response, grain, halation and sharpness are derived here from the physics rather than ported from anywhere. Bundled: pako (MIT/Zlib) and Jost (SIL OFL 1.1) — see LICENSES.md for full terms.
